title: Run-Length Encoding
problem: Given one line of lowercase letters, compress it by writing each run of the same letter in a row as the letter followed by how many times it repeats. For example, aaabccdd becomes a3b1c2d2. A letter that comes back later starts a new run.
starter_code:
# Read one line of lowercase letters.
# Print each run of repeated letters as the letter and its count,
# e.g. aaabccdd -> a3b1c2d2.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Walk through the text keeping track of the current letter and how many times it has repeated in a row.
hints.2: Loop over the letters with a counter. When the letter changes, write out the previous letter and its count, then start a new count. Write out the last run after the loop ends. Counting each letter over the whole text (with a dictionary) is not the same thing: a letter can come back later in a new run.
hints.3:
s = input().strip()
out, i = '', 0
while i < len(s):
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j] == s[i]:
        j += 1
    out += s[i] + str(j - i)
    i = j
print(out)

failure_explanation: Count runs of the same letter in a row, not totals for the whole text: a letter that appears again later starts a new run. Write out the final run after the loop finishes, and write the full count even when it has more than one digit.
